text.arabic_uthmani: وَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَوْلَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ ءَايَةٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ ۗ قُلْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِىٓ إِلَيْهِ مَنْ أَنَابَ

words.gloss_range: resumptive and coordinating opening particle attached to the speech scene

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: ongoing reported speech verb

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah by carrying the prior orientation verdict of 13:26 into a renewed speech confrontation. Because it attaches immediately to {{ar:يَقُولُ}} ({{tr:yaqūlu}}), the connector makes the deniers' saying feel like a continuing manifestation of that prior stance, not a detached report. Its short onset also audibly resets the line before the longer speech verb.

topics.headline: continuity with reopened speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah starts by linking the sign-demand to the prior misplaced orientation rather than introducing a new complaint from nowhere.
topics.reason: The opening particle can resume while linking, and the boundary evidence ties the speech demand to 13:26.

topics.headline: small bound reset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse link is fused to the speech verb and heard as a quick reset before the reported demand unfolds.
topics.reason: The particle is a proclitic on the following verb, so form and pacing support the same opening function.

words.gloss_range: ongoing reported speech introducing a quoted sign-demand
words.root_gloss_range: speech, saying, claiming, and declaring; here the imperfect reports recurring demand-speech

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: genitive Lord-source phrase
commanded prophetic reply

words.prose: {{ar:يَقُولُ}} ({{tr:yaqūlu}}) casts the demand as ongoing speech rather than a single past remark. The verb governs the whole quoted challenge through {{ar:رَّبِّهِۦ}} ({{tr:rabbihī}}), so the sign-demand remains the deniers' utterance, not the narrator's assertion. Its root also frames the ayah's speech contest: their repeated saying is answered by the commanded {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}), while the same sign-demand formula echoes within the surah (13:7; 13:43).

topics.headline: repeated demand-speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the objection is habitual and repeatable, not staged as one isolated historical sentence.
topics.reason: QAC marks the form as imperfect indicative, and the quoted demand is syntactically governed by the speech verb.

topics.headline: full challenge under report
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the whole sign request is framed as spoken challenge rather than neutral inquiry or direct evidence.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the following span as the quoted complement of the verb.

topics.headline: saying answered by say
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a root-level speech pivot: unauthorized recurring claim is answered by authorized commanded speech.
topics.reason: The same speech root appears in the reported demand and the imperative response.

topics.headline: same-surah challenge script
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wording belongs to a recurring same-surah sign-demand script rather than a fresh epistemic concern.
topics.reason: The supplied rows give concrete same-surah witnesses, especially 13:7 and 13:43.

words.gloss_range: definite relative pronoun defining the speaking group by the following denial

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: completed denial defining the speakers

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) introduces the speakers as a known class whose identity waits for {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}). That relative construction turns the following act into definition, so the coming request is heard through a completed denial label rather than through neutral curiosity. The familiar formula also places them within a recurring Quranic antagonist group before the challenge begins.

topics.headline: identity through action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers are grammatically defined by denial before their question is heard.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is completed by the following perfect verb and functions as the subject phrase of the speech verb.

topics.headline: known recurring class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase summons a recognizable antagonist class instead of anonymous questioners.
topics.reason: The definite relative and formula rows support a known recurring class reading.

words.gloss_range: completed collective denial defining the speakers before their demand
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealment, denial, disbelief, and ingratitude; local sense is completed denial with concealment pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: indefinite demanded sign

words.prose: {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) closes the actor phrase with a plural perfect, making denial the completed stance from which the ongoing demand arises. The root's covering image sharpens the irony: those marked by concealment ask for {{ar:ءَايَةٌۭ}} ({{tr:āyatun}}), a marker meant to disclose. Same-surah recurrence (13:7; 13:31) keeps this demand inside a broader pattern of objection.

topics.headline: completed stance before demand
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the request is grounded in an already completed denial-state, not in an open search for evidence.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect plural and completes the relative subject phrase before the demand particle.

topics.headline: covering asks for disclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that a covering-denial root stands just before a demand for a sign whose function is recognition.
topics.reason: The local sense is disbelief, while the root image of covering remains a valid semantic pressure and is reinforced by sign-field pairing.

topics.headline: recurring objection chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the specific challenge contracts a broader diagnosis into a named polemical scene within the surah.
topics.reason: The rows identify same-surah recurrence and a boundary shift from general diagnosis to local confrontation.

words.gloss_range: interrogative reproach particle opening the quoted demand

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: perfect passive descent verb in the demand

words.prose: {{ar:لَوْلَآ}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) launches the quote as reproach: why has a sign not already been sent down? In this context it selects an expectation-gap and challenge force, not a counterfactual 'were it not for' sense. Its long sound holds the demand open before {{ar:أُنزِلَ}} ({{tr:unzila}}) names the absent descent event.

topics.headline: why-not challenge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the deniers are accusing an unmet expectation, not neutrally asking for information.
topics.reason: The particle governs a passive descent demand, so the counterfactual branch is not the local reading.

topics.headline: stretched expectation gap
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pressure of expectation and delay before the demanded descent is named.
topics.reason: The particle's semantic range and pacing rows align with the local challenge force.

words.gloss_range: perfect passive Form IV descent in the demanded revelation event
words.root_gloss_range: descent, sending down, lodging, and staged arrival; here passive caused descent is selected

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: indefinite demanded sign
genitive Lord-source phrase

words.prose: {{ar:أُنزِلَ}} ({{tr:unzila}}) makes the demanded sign the promoted passive subject while leaving the sender unnamed inside the deniers' wording. The perfect passive complains that descent should already have happened, and the {{ar:ن ز ل}} ({{tr:n-z-l}}) root gives the demand a vertical authority axis from {{ar:رَّبِّهِۦ}} ({{tr:rabbihī}}). The wider descent family adds staged-revelation pressure, but the local request packages the sign as a discrete sent-down event; it also echoes earlier surah descent claims (13:1; 13:7). The hamza at the start of {{ar:أُنزِلَ}} ({{tr:unzila}}) and the hamza of {{ar:ءَايَةٌۭ}} ({{tr:āyatun}}) give the demanded descent and sign a clipped, insistent sound.

topics.headline: sign promoted, sender suppressed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the deniers foreground the absent sign while grammatically suppressing the sender they are challenging.
topics.reason: The verb is passive Form IV, and the nominative sign is the passive subject.

topics.headline: authoritative descent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices revelation as vertical authority movement from the Lord-source, while broader lodging or staged branches stay background.
topics.reason: The local passive descent with a source phrase selects the revelation-descent branch and narrows the broader root family.

topics.headline: already-expected event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the impatience of asking for a completed sign-event rather than submitting to staged revelation.
topics.reason: The perfect passive after the reproach particle makes the non-occurrence retrospective.

topics.headline: demand repeats descent frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demand contests a descent-frame the surah has already asserted as true (13:1).
topics.reason: The rows provide concrete same-surah descent witnesses and a convergence claim.

topics.headline: clipped demanded elements
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the hamza catches at descent and sign, giving the challenge a clipped insistence.
topics.reason: The sound row is local and tied to the demanded event and its object.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: toward Him goal phrase

words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) makes the demanded descent land 'upon him,' with the suffix referring to the Prophet. The challenge is therefore personalized around the messenger rather than phrased as a general request for proof. Its vertical 'upon' relation later contrasts with {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}), shifting the ayah from proof demanded upon the Prophet to guidance moving toward God.

topics.headline: descent upon him
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sign-demand targets the prophetic recipient specifically, not proof in the abstract.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence governs the pronoun by the descent verb and resolves the suffix to the Prophet.

topics.headline: upon versus toward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's spatial turn from a sign demanded upon the messenger to guidance directed toward God.
topics.reason: The later matching preposition-plus-pronoun phrase gives this local phrase structural payoff.

topics.headline: recipient compressed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the recipient remains present through a compact suffix without being named directly.
topics.reason: The preposition and suffix form supplies the descent-recipient relation in one bound expression.

words.prose: {{ar:ءَايَةٌۭ}} ({{tr:āyatun}}) is indefinite and nominative, so the deniers ask for an unspecified sign while the passive verb promotes that sign to the grammatical center of the event. Its range covers sign, proof, miracle, and verse, which makes the demand ironic: they ask for a proof-object while the surah is already saturated with signs and opening descent claims (13:1; 13:7). The disputed return/refuge association is not the local sense, but it sharpens the contrast with the ayah's final return criterion in {{ar:أَنَابَ}} ({{tr:anāba}}). Together with {{ar:أُنزِلَ}} ({{tr:unzila}}), the repeated hamza catches make the sign-demand construction audibly pointed.

topics.headline: unspecified passive subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demanded proof is both unspecified and grammatically foregrounded by the passive construction.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as indefinite nominative, and attachment evidence makes it the passive subject.

topics.reason: The local challenge allows miracle-sign while the word's Quranic range also includes verses and proof-bearing signs.

topics.headline: marker with return pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a secondary return/refuge pressure beside the sign-marker sense, connecting the demanded sign to the closing return motif without replacing the local meaning.
topics.reason: The dispute is retained as pressure, but the local noun still functions as the demanded sign.

topics.headline: one sign versus many signs

words.prose: {{ar:مِّن}} ({{tr:min}}) marks {{ar:رَّبِّهِۦ}} ({{tr:rabbihī}}) as the source of the demanded sign. Its source sense is primary here, while the partitive possibility lets the single sign sound like one requested instance from a larger divine sign-repertoire. The phrase also sets up the spatial counterpoint with {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}): from his Lord in the demand, toward Him in the response.

topics.headline: from his Lord
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demand specifies source, not just the existence of a sign.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the genitive Lord phrase as source complement.

words.root_gloss_range: lordship as owning, governing, nurturing, and developing toward completion; local phrase names the demanded source

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: source preposition

words.prose: {{ar:رَّبِّهِۦ}} ({{tr:rabbihī}}) is genitive after {{ar:مِّن}} ({{tr:min}}), so the demanded sign is explicitly sourced from the Prophet's Lord. The suffix keeps that relation in the third person: 'his Lord,' not 'our Lord,' which lets the speakers invoke the Lord-source while distancing themselves from it. The {{ar:ر ب ب}} ({{tr:r-b-b}}) range adds custodial development and governance, so the demand for a sudden spectacle is aimed at the very Lord who manages revelation and formation across the surah.

topics.headline: Lord as demanded source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the source phrase is grammatically bound, definite by possession, and not a loose theological label.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive under the source preposition and bound to the possessive suffix.

topics.headline: his Lord, not ours

topics.reason: The suffix resolves to the Prophet and appears in the deniers' quoted challenge.

topics.headline: managed completion, not spectacle supply
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the Lord-source phrase carries ownership, nurturing, and governance pressure, making the demand for sudden proof theologically charged.
topics.reason: The local noun is Lord, while derivative nurturing imagery remains valid root pressure.

topics.headline: rabb-descent frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase activates a dense revelation-source pairing already present across Surah 13.
topics.reason: The supplied co-occurrence and same-surah rows support the revelation-source frame.

words.gloss_range: second-person masculine singular imperative commanding the prophetic reply
words.root_gloss_range: saying, declaring, and relaying speech; here a clipped imperative authorizes response

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: emphatic assertion particle

words.prose: {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}) is the ayah's hinge: reported human speech gives way to a commanded prophetic reply. Its second-person singular imperative routes the answer through the same messenger targeted by {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}), and its clipped form sharply interrupts the long demand before {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}). The repeated {{ar:ق و ل}} ({{tr:q-w-l}}) root reverses speech authority: they keep saying, but he is told to say.

topics.headline: authorized answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the response is authorized relay, not the Prophet debating on the challengers' terms.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an imperative, and attachment evidence gives the following assertion as its quoted complement.

topics.headline: one addressed messenger

topics.reason: The form is second masculine singular imperative.

topics.headline: demand to answer hinge

topics.reason: The imperative sits between the quoted demand and the emphatic response.

topics.headline: they say, say

topics.reason: The speech-root echo is concrete and local to the demand-response frame.

words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) turns the reply into emphatic assertion. It governs {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}) and scopes over the two orientation outcomes through the ayah's end, so the demand opened by {{ar:لَوْلَآ}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) is answered by certainty rather than by another question. The doubled form marks strengthened news before the named divine agent appears.

topics.headline: certainty over whole reply
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer is framed as settled assertion covering both misguidance and guidance.
topics.reason: The particle governs the divine name and the following predicate.

topics.headline: reproach answered by certainty

topics.reason: The particle contrast structures the demand-response opposition.

topics.headline: strengthened news marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form itself announces strengthened news before the named agent and twin verbs.
topics.reason: The shaddah-bearing particle opens the assertion after the command.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name, accusative under the emphatic particle, governing both outcome verbs
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine-name field with worship/refuge associations and disputed bewilderment pressure; local use is the named divine agent

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}) replaces the deniers' distancing 'his Lord' with the proper divine name. As the accusative subject of {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}), the name is foregrounded before the two opposite verbs, and one named subject governs both {{ar:يُضِلُّ}} ({{tr:yuḍillu}}) and {{ar:يَهْدِىٓ}} ({{tr:yahdī}}). The worship and bewilderment dispute stays secondary, but it fits an ayah about pathlessness and orientation toward the divine agent. The name also concentrates the familiar straying/guidance root pair in one local assertion.

topics.headline: named agent under emphasis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reply names God directly and foregrounds Him grammatically before the outcomes.
topics.reason: The proper name is accusative as the subject governed by the emphatic particle.

topics.headline: one subject, two outcomes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that misguidance and guidance do not come from split sources; both are grammatically governed by one named divine subject.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence carries the divine subject into both coordinated verbs.

topics.headline: his Lord becomes God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the response refuses the deniers' third-person distance and redirects the whole ayah from external proof to divine orientation.
topics.reason: The proper name appears where the answer begins and structures the three-beat demand-response arc.

topics.headline: worship with bewilderment pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices secondary awe and bewilderment pressure around the divine name in a clause about losing and finding the way, without replacing the proper-name sense.
topics.reason: The disputed etymological pressure is meaningful here but cannot override the local proper-name function.

topics.headline: divine name anchors orientation roots
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine name concentrates the co-occurring roots of straying and guidance in one local assertion.
topics.reason: The supplied co-occurrence rows connect the divine name with both orientation outcomes.

words.prose: {{ar:يُضِلُّ}} ({{tr:yuḍillu}}) is imperfect Form IV, so the response names ongoing divine governance of path-loss rather than a static label. Its object is the relative clause {{ar:مَنْ يَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:man yashāʾu}}), keeping the class open and criterion-based. The {{ar:ض ل ل}} ({{tr:ḍ-l-l}}) path-loss image stands opposite {{ar:يَهْدِىٓ}} ({{tr:yahdī}}), and the local formula is marked because 13:27 does not repeat {{ar:يَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:yashāʾu}}) in the guidance limb as 14:4 does. The same root later expands in 13:33, and the doubled lām gives the causative path-loss audible weight.

topics.headline: ongoing action over open class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices misguidance as an ongoing divine action applied to an open relative class.
topics.reason: The imperfect 3ms verb carries the divine subject and takes the relative pronoun as object.

topics.headline: navigational loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices misguidance as loss of way and visibility, while the local clause remains about divinely governed orientation.
topics.reason: The path-loss branch is locally relevant, while hiddenness remains image pressure rather than a replacement gloss.

topics.headline: causative, not God strays

topics.reason: Form IV supports causative force, with active and permissive readings both structurally possible.

topics.headline: loss versus guidance

topics.reason: The paired verbs are coordinated under one subject and supported by dominant co-occurrence rows.

topics.headline: 14:4 symmetry broken

topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows supply concrete comparisons with 14:4 and 13:14.

topics.headline: weighted path-loss

topics.reason: The rows connect the local verb to later same-surah formulation and local sound texture.

words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) after {{ar:يُضِلُّ}} ({{tr:yuḍillu}}) opens the object-domain as 'whomever,' waiting for {{ar:يَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:yashāʾu}}) to supply the criterion. The same pronoun recurs later before {{ar:أَنَابَ}} ({{tr:anāba}}), so the two outcome clauses are parallel in slot but asymmetric in criterion. That repetition makes the shift from will-language to return-language visible.

words.prose: {{ar:يَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:yashāʾu}}) supplies the criterion for the first {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}). The strongest local subject is God from {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}), but the nearby relative pronoun keeps a structurally visible secondary parse in which the human wills; the ambiguity matters because the second limb names {{ar:أَنَابَ}} ({{tr:anāba}}) instead. The object of willing is unexpressed, so the clause foregrounds determining selection itself rather than a named thing willed; the root's thingness association stays as pressure. The imperfect makes will an ongoing criterion crossing from provision in 13:26 into orientation here, and the medial hamza gives the decision point a small audible catch.

topics.headline: divine will with visible ambiguity

topics.reason: Attachment favors God as subject, but the CRITICAL rows preserve a real alternate parse created by the relative frame.

topics.reason: No expressed object follows the will verb in the local clause.

words.prose: {{ar:يَهْدِىٓ}} ({{tr:yahdī}}) inherits {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}) as subject through coordination, but its limb is fuller than a simple mirror of misguidance. It gathers a guided object in {{ar:مَنْ أَنَابَ}} ({{tr:man anāba}}), a destination in {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}), and an ongoing imperfect action responding to completed return. The {{ar:ه د ي}} ({{tr:h-d-y}}) root makes guidance directional, and its gift/offering family adds bestowal and led-movement pressure without replacing the local guidance sense. The long ī of {{ar:يَهْدِىٓ}} ({{tr:yahdī}}) also flows into {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}), letting the sound arc follow the semantic movement toward the goal.

words.prose: {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}) makes the goal of guidance explicit: it moves toward Him, with God as the strongest local antecedent of the suffix. A prophetic referent is structurally possible, but the named divine subject and the following return clause make 'toward God' the controlling reading. The phrase is a compact destination marker and a bookend against {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}): demanded descent upon him gives way to guided return toward Him.

topics.headline: toward Him

topics.reason: The strongest local antecedent is the named divine subject, though the row preserves a structurally possible alternate referent.

topics.headline: guidance as trajectory

topics.reason: The preposition governs the destination complement of the guidance verb.

topics.headline: descent axis to return axis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's spatial theology: proof imagined as coming down upon the Prophet is answered by persons being guided toward God.
topics.reason: The two preposition-plus-pronoun phrases bookend the demand and response.

topics.headline: pronominal destination

topics.reason: The boundary row connects the pronominal goal to the surrounding spatial arc.

words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) in the guidance limb supplies the guided object, but it remains open until {{ar:أَنَابَ}} ({{tr:anāba}}) defines the person by completed return. The repeated pronoun matches the earlier {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}), making the two slots comparable while the criteria diverge: will in the first limb, return in the second. It also anchors the positive traveler category as the ayah moves from provision and orientation into course-correction.

topics.headline: whoever has turned back

topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the pronoun the object of guidance and the following verb its relative clause.

topics.headline: same slot, new criterion

topics.reason: The two man-clauses are locally parallel but completed by different verbs.

topics.headline: returnee as traveler category
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the positive class as a traveler who has turned back, linking the prior provision frame to course-correction.
topics.reason: The boundary row connects the relative class to the journey-provision frame.

words.gloss_range: perfect Form IV return verb closing the guidance criterion

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: toward Him goal phrase

words.prose: {{ar:أَنَابَ}} ({{tr:anāba}}) closes the ayah by defining the guided class as one who has turned back. Its perfect aspect makes the return accomplished, and its Form IV shape presents return as deliberate self-reorientation toward the goal just named by {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}). The rare {{ar:ن و ب}} ({{tr:n-w-b}}) root is concentrated in return-to-God contexts; deputyship and rotation imagery add role-change pressure, but they do not replace repentance or return as the local sense. Against 14:4, this verb is the marked substitute for a second {{ar:يَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:yashāʾu}}). Its open ā landing gives the final return verb closing weight, and the individual singular act resolves the prior provision frame as course-correction.

topics.headline: return completes the class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance is tied to an accomplished human turning while the misguidance limb uses ongoing will-language.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect and completes the relative clause defining the guided object.

topics.headline: deliberate reorientation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices repentance as deliberate reorientation back toward the named goal, not bare regret.
topics.reason: The root image and Form IV morphology support deliberate return, while broader recurrence remains background.

topics.headline: role-change pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a secondary role-change pressure in returning to the Lord, while the local Quranic sense remains return-to-God.
topics.reason: Deputyship is retained as semantic pressure but narrowed because the local and Quranic usage centers return.

topics.headline: marked rare return root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the closing verb as distributionally marked and specialized for return-to-God contexts.
topics.reason: The supplied count and occurrence rows make the root marked without inventing a new local sense.

topics.headline: return replaces second will
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 13:27 introduces human return into the guidance limb where 14:4 has will-language.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows provide the concrete 14:4 formula comparison.

topics.headline: marked closing mechanism
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final verb bears the ayah's closing mechanism with rare-root, form, sound, and directional convergence.
topics.reason: The convergence row ties root image, Form IV, rarity, and the directional goal together.

topics.headline: course-correction after provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a universal category is expressed through an individual act of return and resolves the prior provision frame as course-correction.
topics.reason: The singular perfect under generic relative construction and boundary evidence support this local payoff.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ ... يَهْدِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ أَنَابَ
baseline_models.mechanism: The demand imagines proof as an object delivered downward upon another person; the answer rotates the vector from delivery upon him to guidance toward Him, with return supplying the receiver's movement.

activation_trace.role: Delivery from above supplies the demand's one-way transfer model.
A manifest marker supplies the object the demand expects to inspect.
Gentle direction toward a road changes proof from an object into a trajectory.
Habitual return supplies the responsive movement along that trajectory.

changed_reading.before: The verse answers a request for a fresh externally delivered proof.
changed_reading.after: The answer reverses the demand's geometry: the decisive event is not a sign coming down upon the messenger but a person being directed toward God through return.

baseline_models.mechanism: The request for a visible marker is voiced from a root-field of covering, while straying carries hiddenness and loss. The contrast permits an occlusion model: apparent absence can be produced by the observer's covered orientation rather than by a shortage of markers.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies an active screen between observer and evidence.
Manifest marking supplies what the screen is supposed to make unavailable.
Disappearance and hiddenness render straying as loss from view, not only wrong direction.
Loss supplies the outcome of a covered relation to the sign.

changed_reading.before: The speakers report that no adequate sign is visible.
changed_reading.after: Their visibility test may itself belong to the misguidance mechanism: covering turns a present marker into something hidden or lost.

baseline_models.mechanism: The paired speech verbs stage a contest over framing. The objection proposes negotiation over what the Lord must supply; the imperative answer declines that test and relocates the issue in divine willing and the speaker's direction of return.

activation_trace.role: Negotiation over an affair makes the two utterances rival framings of the same test.
Speech as held position makes the demand an epistemic stance rather than a neutral request.
Will attached to its object replaces the speakers' proposed control over the evidentiary terms.
Approach in distance supplies the alternative test: whether one comes near rather than dictates a display.

changed_reading.before: The answer explains why the requested sign has not appeared.
changed_reading.after: The answer contests who defines an adequate sign and turns the proposed test of the messenger into a test of the questioner's orientation.

baseline_models.mechanism: Two return inventories converge on recurrence, while another branch adds proximity. The form can therefore carry a repeated reorientation toward God rather than only a completed one-time reversal.

activation_trace.role: A recurrent turn supplies iterative rather than punctual return.
Repeated return to a place reinforces the iterative spatial pattern.
Nearness turns recurrence into progressive approach.
Direction and manner of travel give repeated return a stable heading.

changed_reading.before: Guidance follows a single decisive act of turning back.
changed_reading.after: Guidance accompanies a recurrent nearward reorientation whose constancy lies in direction, not in never deviating.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah opens by naming plural markers in the Book and declaring what was sent down from the Lord to be reality-matching truth. The later singular demand therefore occurs inside an already populated sign-field and changes from a report of absence into a rejection of available form.

activation_trace.role: The demanded manifest marker anchors the focus question.
Plural manifest markers establish that the context already recognizes signs.
Ordered letters and their written product give those markers a textual embodiment.
Completed delivery duplicates the very descent the objection says it lacks.
Stable correspondence with reality assigns evidentiary weight to the delivered text.

structural_cues: 13:1 precedes the demand with plural signs, the Book, and the same descent-from-Lord sequence; 13:7 then repeats the demand before 13:27.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: textual signs, descent, and truth are explicitly conjoined before the repeated demand. Reader: the demand discounts an already supplied mode of sign. Alternative: the speakers may be asking for a different, spectacular class of sign rather than denying all signs.

changed_reading.before: A requested sign has simply not been sent.
changed_reading.after: Signs have already descended in textual form; the live dispute concerns which form the speakers will count as a sign.

context_deltas.mechanism: The doubled change construction in 13:11 places divine change and change within persons on two sides of one relation. It strengthens the focus coupling of divine guidance with human return and makes willing legible as responsive governance without dissolving divine initiative.

activation_trace.role: Divine willing anchors the side of the relation that the context must not erase.
Return supplies the human reorientation paired with guidance.
Twice-repeated alteration supplies reciprocal movement across the divine-human relation.
The inward faculty of mind and awareness locates the receptive change within persons.

structural_cues: 13:11 repeats change on divine and human sides and places the second change within themselves; 13:27 similarly couples God's guiding with the person's return.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: two change clauses and the focus's guidance-return condition are explicit. Reader: inward reorientation is treated as opening reception to guidance. Alternative: 13:11 may state a separate social law and leave 'whom He wills' unexplained.

changed_reading.before: Whom God guides or misguides is an opaque selection unrelated to the person's state.
changed_reading.after: The selection can coexist with a reciprocal reception grammar: change within and return toward God are the human side of a divinely governed transition.

context_deltas.mechanism: A single visible flash produces opposed affects, and an overwhelming strike coexists with dispute about God under the same willing formula. Spectacular intensity therefore does not mechanically standardize response.

activation_trace.role: The demanded visible marker anchors the proposed coercive spectacle.
A brilliant flash supplies a concrete, immediately visible sign-event.
Anticipatory fear supplies one response to the same flash.
Heartfelt hope supplies the opposed response without changing the stimulus.
The crashing event from above supplies a maximal public spectacle.
Entwined contention shows argument persisting alongside the spectacle.
The repeated willing formula binds the spectacle sequence back to the focus answer.

structural_cues: 13:12-13 moves from seeing lightning, through fear and hope, to thunderbolts and continued disputation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: one flash has divergent affects, and a thunderbolt is followed by dispute. Reader: these are evidence that spectacle cannot compel one reading. Alternative: the phenomena may display power without directly modeling the requested sign.

changed_reading.before: A sufficiently dramatic sign would settle the dispute.
changed_reading.after: Even intense visible events divide affect and permit continued argument; guidance cannot be reduced to increasing spectacle.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same descent becomes flow received by differently measured channels; conspicuous foam rises but leaves, while useful material remains. This supplies a hydraulic reception model for guidance and a reversal of the demand's visual criterion: what is most elevated and visible may be least durable.

activation_trace.role: Demanded delivery anchors the focus to the analogy's descending input.
Delivered water supplies one common input to multiple receivers.
Flow turns descent into movement through a receptive system.
A channel for floodwater supplies receiver-specific capacity.
Measured limit makes reception vary by the channel's actual extent.
Floating froth supplies the highly visible but separable surface layer.
Increase and elevation explain why the disposable layer attracts attention.
Benefit supplies a criterion distinct from visual prominence.
Stable remaining identifies durable reception as the analogy's successful outcome.

structural_cues: 13:17 explicitly sequences one descent, differently measured valleys, rising foam, its removal, and the remaining benefit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: common water, measured channels, floating foam, and remaining benefit are explicit. Reader: water models delivered guidance and foam models spectacular surface evidence. Alternative: the analogy may distinguish truth and falsehood generally without specifying sign-demand or reception psychology.

changed_reading.before: One externally delivered proof should affect every observer alike.
changed_reading.after: What descends is received according to capacity; the spectacular surface can pass away while guidance is recognized by what is retained and becomes useful.

context_deltas.mechanism: Knowing the descent as truth is opposed to inward blindness and followed by remembering, fulfilling, connecting, patience, worship, spending, and repelling harm. The sequence expands return from a private mental pivot into a maintained network of practices and relations.

activation_trace.role: Recurrent return anchors the focus process being socially expanded.
Delivered revelation supplies the object known rather than merely demanded.
Blindness of inward perception marks the failed alternative to knowing the descent.
Recollection after possible forgetfulness gives return a renewable cognitive practice.
Maintained connection and refusal of severance externalize return in durable relations.
The negative sequence makes broken connection the practical inverse of sustained return.

structural_cues: 13:19-22 runs from knowing and remembering through covenant, connection, patience, prayer, spending, and repelling harm; 13:25 reverses the sequence through rupture.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: cognitive recognition is followed by a concrete practice sequence and its inverse. Reader: that sequence unfolds what return looks like over time. Alternative: it may describe the guided group without defining the mechanism of their initial guidance.

changed_reading.before: Turning back is an inward and largely private decision.
changed_reading.after: Return is sustained as remembering, keeping bonds, and repeatedly enacting a connected moral pattern; rupture is its practical opposite.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's recurrent return is followed immediately by hearts settling through remembrance, a good place of return, and the messenger's own declaration of reliance and return to Him. The sequence forms a loop: a turnable center repeatedly reorients, remembrance damps its motion, and reliance holds the destination.

activation_trace.role: Recurring return supplies the loop's repeated reorientation.
Repeated settling supplies the loop's stabilizing outcome.
Turning a thing from its face makes the heart a reversible center requiring reorientation.
Repeated recollection supplies the feedback that restores orientation.
Return to a destination turns the process into an arrival-pattern, not mere retreat.
Reliant trust supplies the posture that holds the repeated turn toward its destination.

structural_cues: 13:27 ends with guidance 'to Him' for one who returns; 13:28 repeats heart-settling, 13:29 names a good return-place, and 13:30 ends 'to Him is my return.'
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: adjacency, repeated settling, remembrance, return-place, reliance, and the repeated 'to Him' direction are explicit. Reader: they form a stabilizing feedback loop. Alternative: settling and destination may be consequences of return rather than its internal mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Return is a one-time repentance that precedes guidance.
changed_reading.after: Return is a recurrent orientation of a turnable heart, stabilized through remembrance and reliance toward a named destination.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context imagines a recitation that displaces solid mountains, cuts earth, and makes the lifeless speak, then immediately returns all command and universal guidance to God's will. The escalation denies that guidance is a mechanical threshold reached by making a sign sufficiently spectacular.

activation_trace.role: The demanded marker anchors the counterfactual as an answer to spectacle-seeking.
Set movement supplies the first impossible-scale transformation.
Elevated solidity makes that movement a test against apparent immovability.
Intelligible speech between parties supplies the counterfactual voice of the dead.
Loss of life makes speech the maximal reversal of ordinary capacity.
Severed expectation marks the believers' relinquishment of compulsory universal response.
Divine willing repeats the focus formula after the maximal-sign sequence.
Guiding everyone names the result no spectacle can independently compel.

structural_cues: 13:31 escalates movement of mountains, rupture of earth, and speech of the dead, then pivots to all command belonging to God and the possibility of guiding everyone.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: the counterfactual escalation and the will-guidance pivot are adjacent. Reader: the sequence severs spectacle from compulsory guidance. Alternative: it may emphasize divine power and ownership of command without making a general claim about evidence psychology.

changed_reading.before: The requested miracle would produce belief if only it were dramatic enough.
changed_reading.after: Even the imagined maximum of physical and biological reversal does not control guidance; the focus answer rejects spectacle as an independent causal lever.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later recurrence of misguidance is preceded by made-attractive scheming and diversion from an extended road, then followed by the absence of a guide. This unfolds the compact focus contrast into a mediated path process: valuation is altered, the traveler is turned aside, and loss of guidance is the resulting state under divine agency.

activation_trace.role: Departure from guidance and intended direction anchors the focus outcome.
Making something appear good supplies altered valuation before the path event.
Active turning-away supplies the transition from attractive framing to displacement.
A traversable extended road supplies the route from which diversion occurs.
Covering links altered appearance to the focus speakers' occluded stance.
The repeated loss of intended direction names the chain's governed result.
Absence of gentle road-direction closes the mechanism in the same terms as the focus.

structural_cues: 13:33 orders beautification, scheming, diversion from the road, divine misguidance, and no guide in one clause sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: altered attractiveness, diversion, road, misguidance, and no guide are sequential. Reader: the earlier clauses mediate the later state. Alternative: the clauses may list parallel features rather than a strict causal chain.

changed_reading.before: Divine misguidance is an unexplained instantaneous assignment.
changed_reading.after: Misguidance can be traced as a governed process in which attractive framing and diversion reorganize a person's relation to the road, while the text still assigns the final state to God.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same willing formula later sits between erasure and confirmation in relation to a master writing. Read back into the focus, misguidance and guidance need not be imagined as two permanently sealed labels; return can mark a transition within a trace whose effects may be removed or made stable.

activation_trace.role: Willing attached to an object anchors the repeated formula.
Return supplies a plausible transition rather than a permanent category.
Removal of an effect supplies reversibility in the later willing formula.
The repeated object-directed will explicitly governs erasure and confirmation.
Durable stability supplies the opposite possible operation to erasure.
Binding inscription supplies the substrate on which removal and stabilization are imagined.

structural_cues: 13:39 places 'what He wills' directly between erasing and confirming and ends with the source Book.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: will governs paired erasure and confirmation in a writing frame. Reader: this makes guidance states dynamically revisable. Alternative: the operations may concern decrees or textual records without licensing application to personal guidance.

changed_reading.before: Guided and misguided are static identities fixed once assigned.
changed_reading.after: The categories may be dynamically administered traces: return opens a change whose prior effect can be erased and whose new orientation can be stabilized.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah closes with the same they-say/say frame, but the denial of the messenger is answered by sufficient testimony and knowledge of the Book. This completes the focus reframing: evidentiary adequacy moves from a demanded display to witness, disclosed knowledge, and textual intelligibility.

activation_trace.role: The focus negotiation anchors the disputed standard of evidence.
The repeated speech exchange closes the same negotiation at surah scale.
Declared sufficiency directly supplies a replacement criterion for enough evidence.
Testimony grounded in knowledge supplies evidentiary force without spectacle.
Disclosure to a knower supplies an epistemic mode of sign-recognition.
The written composition returns the closure to the textual sign-field opened in 13:1.

structural_cues: 13:43 repeats the paired speech frame and places sufficiency, witness, knowledge, and the Book in its answer.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: the closing denial and answer use the focus speech pattern and name sufficient witness plus Book-knowledge. Reader: this resolves the sign dispute by changing the evidentiary mode. Alternative: the closure answers denial of messengership specifically, not every possible request in 13:27.

changed_reading.before: Only a visible extraordinary token could answer the speakers' challenge.
changed_reading.after: The surah's answer develops an alternative economy of evidence: textual signs, knowledgeable witness, and transformed orientation can be sufficient without the demanded spectacle.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the non-dominant ق ل ل mapping under the paired speech root and connects it to the adjacent heart sequence. It remains anchored in both focus speech tokens and the focus return verb, with context support from repeated settling. Render only as a mapped-root resonance or dynamical analogy, never as the lexical translation of يقول or قل.

activation_trace.role: Instability and motion make the paired speeches oscillating rival framings.
Recurring return supplies corrective cycles rather than one final exchange.
Reversal of a thing's face makes the receiving center capable of repeated flips.
Settling supplies the damping state reached through remembrance.

changed_reading.before: The paired sayings are a stable objection followed by a stable answer.
changed_reading.after: At the level of exploratory root resonance, the verse stages oscillating framings that are not resolved by louder speech but damped through recurrent return and heart-settling.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because it activates the non-dominant ه د د inventory beneath يهدي. It remains anchored to the exact focus guidance token and gains contextual pressure from the imagined movement of solid mountains. Downstream prose must label it a destructive resonance within guidance, not translate يهدي as breaking.

activation_trace.role: Severe breaking supplies a disruptive edge to the otherwise gentle guidance field.
Return keeps the disruptive resonance tied to reorientation rather than destruction for its own sake.
Displacement supplies contextual movement of what appears fixed.
Hardness that stops excavation supplies the resistant posture that guidance may have to disrupt.

changed_reading.before: Guidance only indicates an already traversable road.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, guidance can include breaking the hardened evidentiary posture that prevents return, after which direction becomes possible.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-domain reading uses the pigment branch under مكر, which is materially vivid but not the ordinary sense of the verse's scheming term. It remains anchored through the focus covering and hiddenness roots and the explicit 13:33 sequence of beautification, scheming, diversion, road, and misguidance. Render as a coloring-layer analogy, not as a lexical equation of plot with pigment.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the focus substrate on which a deceptive surface layer can operate.
Hiddenness supplies the perceptual result of the applied layer.
Made attractiveness supplies the polished appearance of the misleading layer.
Red pigment supplies a material analogy for coloring what the traveler sees.
Diversion converts the colored perception into changed movement.
The extended road remains the concealed or abandoned directional reference.

changed_reading.before: Misguidance is simply choosing the wrong road.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, an attractive coloring layer covers the road's appearance, so altered perception produces diversion before the road is consciously rejected.

strongest_changes: The demand for a sign is revised by the surah's opening claim that plural textual signs have already descended as truth.
The descent/return vector reverses proof from an object delivered upon the messenger into a guided trajectory toward God.
The water-and-foam analogy changes equal external delivery into measured reception, durable benefit, and disposable spectacle.
The maximal-sign counterfactual separates spectacular force from compulsory guidance.
The beautification-diversion-road sequence unfolds misguidance as a mediated process while retaining divine agency.
summary.what_was_special: The focus held several readings at once: evidentiary form, directional reversal, perceptual covering, recurrent return, social enactment, affective stabilization, and mediated path loss. Non-dominant mappings preserved additional resonances of oscillation and disruptive breaking, while the pigment branch made covering materially inspectable rather than collapsing it into a generic theme.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet does not settle how divine willing and reciprocal human change are causally ordered.
The hydraulic analogy explicitly models truth and falsehood, but its application to sign reception remains reader-supplied.
The heart-as-reversal, speech-as-oscillation, guidance-as-breaking, and pigment readings are branch-valid but intentionally form-distant.
The erasure/confirmation frame may concern decree or writing without directly revising personal guidance states.
The closing witness-and-Book answer may address denial of messengership more narrowly than the sign demand.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. `ن و ب/B001` is habitual return and recurring turn. Guidance points `إِلَيْهِ` to one who returns, and 13:28–30 unfolds remembrance, action, and `مَتَاب`. I infer a maintained orientation rather than one reversal; `أَنَابَ` enters a recurrent guidance loop.
2. `ه د ي/B002` is course and intended direction. The demand for an object-sign is answered with trajectory. I infer that guidance is evidenced by changed course, not spectacle alone.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The repeated return language of 13:29–30 confirmed recurrence, while 13:31 again denied autonomous efficacy to spectacle.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The answer to sign-demand is a return-path.** `ض ل ل / B001` is going astray from guidance and aim, `ض ل ل / B002` is being hidden or disappearing, `ه د ي / B001` is gentle guidance toward a way, and `ن و ب / B001` is habitual return and recurring turn. The demand seeks an object sent down, but the response shifts to motion: loss of way versus guidance toward God for one who turns back. Nearby 13:28 repeatedly settles turning hearts through remembrance, 13:29 names a good return-place, 13:30 ends in trust and return, and 13:31 contrasts spectacular transformations with guidance. I assign disappearance the role of loss from the navigable field and recurring return the role of re-entering it. The packet supplies the two directions; I infer enacted return -> opened guidance route. The ayah reads guidance as reciprocal orientation rather than possession of a spectacle.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 13:28-30 unexpectedly repeat the return mechanism as settled hearts, `مآب`, and `متاب`. This lexical clustering confirmed that `أناب` is not a momentary pivot but recurring orientation sustained through remembrance, action, and trust.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Related persons are joined, admitted, and settled together in a protected dwelling.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Lineage and architecture converge through acts of joining and admission.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Entry, Gates, and Settled Residence
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: The household enters a planted enclosure through gates and takes up a stable station in safety.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: tree-covered garden (`quranic:root_000266:B003/m01`); entry into an interior (`quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`); gate as entrance (`quranic:root_000163:B001/m01`); home and settled station (`quranic:root_001492:B003/m01`); residence in a place (`quranic:root_001273:B006/m01`); safety and freedom from harm (`quranic:root_000737:B001/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 13:22 `أَقَامُوا` (ق و م); 13:23 `جَنَّات` (ج ن ن), `يَدْخُلُون` (د خ ل), and `بَاب` (ب و ب); 13:24 `سَلَام` (س ل م); 13:27 `أُنْزِلَ` (ن ز ل).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Garden, entrance, gate, station, and safety make a coherent arrival scene. Peace is the condition of the inhabited interior, not a detached salutation.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P2 - Return, Guidance, and Entrusted Reliance
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A person turns toward a destination, follows guidance, and entrusts the journey's care to a dependable custodian.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Repentance becomes recurrent homeward movement, and trust becomes delegated care rather than passivity.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Recurrent Homeward Turn
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: One who has departed repeatedly turns back toward a known destination.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: recurrent return to a place (`quranic:root_001562:B001/m01`); return to a home or destination (`quranic:root_000065:B001/m01`); invitation to turn back in repentance (`quranic:root_000189:B003/m01`); turning and final destination (`quranic:root_001248:B005/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Turning, returning, and arriving at a homeward endpoint make repentance spatial and iterative. The path can be re-entered because return remains an available operation.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P2 - Return, Guidance, and Entrusted Reliance
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A person turns toward a destination, follows guidance, and entrusts the journey's care to a dependable custodian.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Repentance becomes recurrent homeward movement, and trust becomes delegated care rather than passivity.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Guided Route Under Trusted Care
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A guide indicates the road while a trusted guardian receives responsibility for the traveler's affair.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: gentle guidance to road and truth (`quranic:root_001583:B001/m01`); delegation of an affair (`quranic:root_001681:B001/m01`); reliance on another (`quranic:root_001681:B002/m01`); custodian sufficient to guard what is entrusted (`quranic:root_001681:B006/m01`); lordship as care and mastery (`quranic:root_000532:B001/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 13:27 `يَهْدِي` (ه د ي) and `رَبّه` (ر ب ب); 13:30 `رَبِّي` (ر ب ب) and `تَوَكَّلْتُ` (و ك ل); 13:31 `هَدَى` (ه د ي).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Guidance supplies direction; entrustment supplies dependable care. Reliance therefore completes rather than replaces the act of turning toward the destination.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P2 - Effective Utterance and Transformed Terrain
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Recited communication is imagined as an operative force capable of moving, cutting, or awakening its object.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Voice-following, inscription, movement, incision, and revived dialogue become distinct operations of effective speech.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Recitation and Transmission
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Revealed information is carried by a messenger and voiced in a following sequence to hearers.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: reading and recitation (`quranic:root_001210:B002/m01`); a second voice following the first (`quranic:root_000186:B007/m01`); divine message and inspiration (`quranic:root_001633:B004/m01`); messenger and message (`quranic:root_000563:B002/m01`); delivery of book or communication downward (`quranic:root_001492:B002/m02`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 13:30 `أَرْسَلْنَاك` (ر س ل), `لِتَتْلُو` (ت ل و), and `أَوْحَيْنَا` (و ح ي); 13:31 `قُرْآن` (ق ر ء); 13:27 `أُنْزِلَ` (ن ز ل).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Message, messenger, descent, leading voice, and following voice form a transmission chain. Recitation is the audible continuation of revelation.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı sesle ortaya çıkarılan söz ve harflerden kurulu sözlü ifade olarak verir. Geçici çerçeve aynı çekirdeği taşıyor; dil organı, hükümdar unvanı ve mecazi yan kullanımlar bu dalın dışında kalır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal çıplak söz söyleme ve söylenmiş söz çekirdeğidir; organ, unvan, söylenti ve mecazlar ayrı dallardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam bare olduğu için tanım çıplak söyleme ve sözlü ifade anlamıyla sınırlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir düşünceyi veya sözü sesli biçimde dışa vurma ve böyle dışa vurulmuş harfli sözlü ifade anlamıdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek işlem, sözü sesli olarak dışa çıkarmaktır.
Söylenen şey tek söz, cümle, şiir veya konuşma ölçeğinde olabilir.
Ad biçimleri aynı söylenmiş söz alanında toplanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, sözü sesle dışa çıkarılan ve harflerden oluşan sözlü ifade çekirdeğinde toplar; ad biçimleri de aynı alana bağlıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sözü sesli biçimde ortaya koyma ve ortaya konmuş sözlü ifade için genel başlık olarak uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Fiilsel söyleme işlemini korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi ilgili biçimi doğrudan konuşma organı olan dil diye açıklar. Geçici çerçeve bu organ anlamını doğru taşır ve söylenmiş söz ya da söz sahibi anlamlarını bu dalın dışında bırakır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi belirli bir eski bölgesel yönetici unvanını, çoğullarını, kadın biçimini ve sözü geçerli kişi açıklamasını birlikte verir. Geçici çerçeve, sıradan söz anlamı değil unvan ve otorite anlamı olduğunu doğru sınırlar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam collocation olduğu için tanım yalnız verilen yalan ve isnat kalıplarına bağlıdır.

facets.statement: Bir varlığın sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından çok olmayışıdır.
Azlık, kişinin yoksullaşması veya toplum içinde düşük ve değersiz görülmesi sonucuna uzanabilir.
Bir şeyi gerçekte ya da değerlendiren kişinin gözünde az sayma ve az gösterme anlamını taşır.
Belirli olumsuzluk ve sıklık yapılarında hiç yokluğu veya bir eylemin pek seyrek gerçekleşmesini anlatır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yükü taşıma veya taşıyabilme ile öznenin yükselip harekete geçmesini aynı kolda açıkça toplar; kuşun uçuşa kalkması, göğün yükselmesi ve yolcuların yüklenip ayrılması ayrı katılımcı gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Taşıma, yükselme ve yüklenerek yola koyulma bu kolun sınırıdır; salt sayısal azlık bu anlamlara katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yük taşıma ile yükselme çekirdek çizgileri ayrılır; ağır bulut taşıma, uçuşa kalkma ve yolcuların ayrılması yalnızca kendi özne ve yapılarında geçerlidir.

concept_map.definition: Bir yükü kaldırıp taşıyabilmeyi veya üstlenmeyi ve bir öznenin yükselerek harekete geçmesini bildirir. İkinci çizgi kuşun uçuşa kalkmasını, göğün yükselmesini ve yolcuların yüklenip yola koyulmasını kapsar.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi kaldıracak gücü bulmak, onu taşımak veya yük olarak üstlenmektir.
Bir öznenin aşağıdaki konumundan yükselmesi veya kuş gibi harekete ve uçuşa başlamasıdır.
Yolcuların yüklerini alıp bulundukları yerden ayrılarak yolculuğa başlamasıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir yükü kaldırıp taşıma ile yukarı kalkarak harekete geçme çizgilerini bir araya getirir; kuş, gök, bulut ve yolcu örnekleri katılımcıya göre bu iki çizgiyi somutlaştırır.

concept_gloss.text: yük kaldırma, yükselme ve yola koyulma
concept_gloss.applicability: Taşıma, yukarı kalkma ve yüklenerek hareket etme çizgilerinin birlikte özetlenmesi gereken kavram haritasında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yük üstlenme, yükselme ve yolculuk için harekete geçme bileşenlerini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin veya başka bir taşıyıcının bir nesnenin ağırlığını üstlenmesi bağlamında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yükü kaldırma gücü ile onu fiilen taşıma anlamlarını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Göğün yükselmesi veya kuşun uçuşa kalkması gibi yukarı yönlü hareket bağlamlarında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yukarı kalkma ile uçuş için yerden ayrılma değerlerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir topluluğun yolculuk yüklerini alarak bulunduğu yerden ayrılması bağlamına özgüdür.

error_profile.preserves: Yük alma, ayrılma ve yolculuğa başlama aşamalarını birlikte korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol yükü taşımanın yanında yükselme, havalanma ve yüklenerek ayrılma anlamlarını da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol yükü taşıma eyleminden çok onu taşıyacak güce sahip olmayı öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da bir yükün ağırlığını karşılayacak gücü ve taşıma yeterliğini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Taşıma yeterliği ortak olsa da bu kol fiilî taşıma ve yerden yükselme yönlerine açılır; komşu kol güç yetirme sınırında kalır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol yük üstlenmeyi, kuşun havalanmasını ve yolcuların yüklenerek ayrılmasını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol kişinin oturduğu yerden kalkmasını ve bir nesneyi bulunduğu yerden kaldırmayı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki kol da aşağıdaki veya durağan bir konumdan kalkma ve hareket başlangıcını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kol yükselmeyi taşıma ve yolculukla bağlar; komşu kol bedensel olarak ayağa kalkma ve nesneyi yerinden kaldırma çevresindedir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kolda yolculuk anlamı yolcuların yüklerini alıp bulundukları yerden ayrılmasıyla sınırlıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol yol üzerinde ilerlemeyi ve belirli bir hedefe doğru seyahat etmeyi genel olarak bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da bir yerden ayrılarak yolculuğa başlama durumunda buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kol başlangıçtaki yüklenme ve kalkış anını anlatır; komşu kol yolculuğun kendisini ve hedefe doğru ilerlemeyi çekirdek edinir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; taşıma gücü, yerden kalkma ve yolculuğa başlama komşuları bu kolun üç kurucu yönünü en az yinelemeyle açıklar.
branches.what_is_ar: حمل الشيء واحتماله، وارتفاعه أو نهوضه، وارتحال القوم ظاعنين
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس مجرد القلة العددية، ولا قلة الجبل، ولا الرعدة
branches.source_phrase_ar: أقل الجرة أطاق حملها؛ استقلت السماء ارتفعت؛ استقل القوم مضوا وارتحلوا (sihah)؛ أقل الرجل الشيء واستقله إذا احتمله؛ استقل الطائر إذا نهض للطيران؛ استقل النبات أناف؛ استقل القوم إذا احتملوا ظاعنين؛ أقلت سحابا ثقالا أي حملت؛ قل إذا رفع وقل إذا علا (tahdhib)؛ أقلت سحابا ثقالا أي احتملته؛ أقللت كذا وجدته قليل المحمل (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kişiyi korku veya öfke yüzünden tutan titreme ve silkinişi açıkça tanımlar; genel hareket kararsızlığı değil, duygusal tetikleyicisi bulunan bedensel bir sarsıntı söz konusudur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol insanda korku veya öfkeyle beliren titremeyle sınırlıdır; nesnelerin genel sallanma ve yerinde duramama hali ayrı koldadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Duygudan doğan titreme temel addır; kişiyi titremenin tutması ve öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi yalnızca ilgili yapılara bağlı anlatımlardır.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın korku veya öfke yüzünden titremesi, ürpermesi ya da bedensel olarak silkelenmesidir. Durum, kişiyi bir titreme nöbetinin tutması veya öfkenin titremeyle dışa vurulması biçiminde anlatılabilir.

facets.statement: İnsan bedeninde beliren titreme, ürperti veya istemsiz silkiniş halidir.
Titremenin belirleyici nedeni korku ya da öfkedir.
Belirli yapılarda titremenin kişiyi tutması veya kişinin öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar insandaki titreme ve silkinişte birleşir; korku ile öfke başlıca nedenlerdir ve durum hem kişiyi tutan bir nöbet hem öfkenin bedensel belirtisi olarak anlatılır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Duygusal nedeni ve bedensel titremeyi birlikte taşıyan bütün kol için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Korku veya öfke koşulunu ve bunun doğurduğu bedensel titremeyi birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Korkunun yol açtığı kısa ve istemsiz bedensel titreme bağlamında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Korkuya bağlı istemsiz titreme ve silkiniş hissini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Titremenin kişiyi birden tutan belirgin bir durum olarak anlatıldığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Titremenin kişiyi tutan bedensel bir olay olarak sunuluşunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Öfkenin bedensel titreme halinde dışa vurulduğu kişi bağlamlarına özgüdür.

error_profile.preserves: Öfke nedenini ve onunla birlikte ortaya çıkan titremeyi korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol titremenin korku veya öfkeden doğmasını anlam sınırının parçası yapar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol insandaki titreme veya silkinişi belirli bir duygusal nedenle sınırlamaz.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da insan bedeninde ortaya çıkan titreme veya silkinişi adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bedensel olay aynıdır; bu kol korku ve öfke koşulunu taşırken komşu kart neden bakımından daha genel kalır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol korkunun yanında öfkeyi de titremenin belirleyici nedeni olarak içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol hastalık, gevşeklik, yumuşaklık ve korkaklıkla ilişkili titremeleri de kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki kol da özellikle korku sırasında insanda görülen titreme ve ürpermede örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Korkuya bağlı kullanımda yakınlaşırlar; bu kol öfkeyi ekler, komşu kol ise hastalık ve bedensel gevşeklik gibi başka nedenlere açılır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar incelendi; genel insan titremesi ve nedenleri daha geniş ürperme alanı, bu kolun kişi ve duygu sınırını en iyi gösterir.

branches.source_phrase_ar: القل الرعدة والانتفاض؛ أخذ فلانا القل إذا أخذته رعدة من فزع (jamhara)؛ القل بالكسر شبه الرعدة؛ أخذه قل من الغضب (sihah)؛ القل الرعدة؛ أخذه قل إذا أرعد من الغضب؛ إذا غضب قد استقل (tahdhib)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyi hareket ettirip sallandırma, nesnenin bulunduğu yerde kararlı duramaması ve hareketin çıkardığı sesi birlikte verir; bunlar tek bir fiziksel hareket olayının neden, sonuç ve işitsel yönleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol genel fiziksel oynama, kararsızlık ve hareket sesiyle ilgilidir; korku veya öfkeden doğan insana özgü titreme değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım çıplak kolun hareket ettirme, sallanma, yerinde duramama ve hareket sesi anlamlarını kapsar; özel bir yapının anlamı genelleştirilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi hareket ettirerek yerinden oynatmayı ve onun kararsızca sallanıp bulunduğu yerde duramamasını bildirir; bu hareketin çıkardığı ses de aynı olayın işitsel yönüdür.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi hareket ettirip onun yerinden oynamasına ve sarsılmasına neden olmaktır.
Nesnenin bulunduğu yerde sabit kalmayıp sallanması, oynaması veya düzensiz hareket etmesidir.
Sallanma ve yer değiştirme sırasında çıkan ses, hareket olayının işitsel belirtisi olarak adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar dışarıdan hareket ettirme ile nesnenin kararsızca sallanıp yerinde duramaması üzerinde birleşir; hareketin sesi bu fiziksel olayın ayrılmaz işitsel belirtisi olarak eklenir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Neden olunan hareketi ve nesnenin ortaya çıkan kararsız sallanmasını birlikte kapsayan temel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Hareket ettirme nedenini ve sabit kalamayan nesnenin sallanma sonucunu birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin bir nesneyi hareket ettirerek onun oynamasına ve sarsılmasına neden olduğu bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Dışarıdan uygulanan hareketi ve nesnenin sarsılması sonucunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir nesnenin gevşeklik veya kararsızlık nedeniyle bulunduğu yerde sabit kalmadığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Sabit kalamama ile düzensiz sallanma durumunu birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sallanan veya oynayan nesnenin çıkardığı sesin adlandırıldığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Sesin genel bir ses değil, hareketten doğan işitsel belirti oluşunu korur.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol kalp, deniz, diş, ağaç ve gök gürültüsü gibi alanlardaki şiddetli sarsıntıyı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da bir nesneyi hareket ettirip onun sallanmasına veya sarsılmasına neden olmayı anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Fiziksel sarsılma alanı yakındır; bu kol hareket ettirme, sabit kalamama ve hareket sesini kurarken komşu kol farklı varlıklardaki şiddetli sarsıntıyı öne çıkarır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kolda ses, nesnenin kararsız hareketi ve sallanmasının sonucu olarak ortaya çıkar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol çan, gök gürültüsü ve bulut gibi kaynaklardan gelen çınlama ve gürleme seslerini de kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki kol da bir nesnenin hareketi sırasında ortaya çıkan işitilebilir sesi içerebilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kolun çekirdeği fiziksel kararsızlık ve sallanmadır, ses ikincildir; komşu kolda ses ve çınlama daha bağımsız bir anlam alanı oluşturur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol nesnenin oynatılması, yerinde duramaması ve hareket sesiyle ilgilidir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol insanda korku veya öfke yüzünden ortaya çıkan titremeyi bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da gözle görülen düzensiz bir sarsılma veya titreme görünümü taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kolda nesne ve fiziksel kararsızlık kurucudur; komşu kolda insan bedeni ile korku veya öfke nedeni kurucudur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; genel sallama, hareketten doğan ses ve aynı kökteki duygusal titreme karşılaştırmaları fiziksel hareket çekirdeğinin sınırını en açık biçimde gösterir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi örtme ve görünmez kılma çekirdeğini; zırhı giysiyle kaplama, silahla örtünme, külün toprakla kapanması ve yıldızların güneş ışığında görünmemesi gibi gerçekleşmelerle açıkça destekler.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek fiziksel örtmedir; dinî inkâr, nimeti yadsıma ve günahı giderme bu dala girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın örtme çekirdeğini korur; zırh, silah, kül ve gök cisimleriyle ilgili kullanımlar bu çekirdeğin yapıya bağlı gerçekleşmeleri olarak ayrılır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi başka bir şeyle örterek görünmesini engellemek veya kapalı duruma getirmektir. Zırhın giysiyle, kişinin silahla ya da külün savrulan toprakla örtülmesi bu işlemin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesnenin üstünü kapatarak onu görünmez veya örtülü duruma getirme işlemi.
Zırhı giysiyle kaplama, silahla örtünme ve külün üstünün toprakla kapanması çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.
Güneşin yıldızları görünmez kılması da görsel örtme sonucu üzerinden bu çekirdeğe bağlanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar örtme ve kapatma çekirdeğinde birleşir; farklı örnekler bu işlemin nesne, giysi, silah, kül ve gök görünümü üzerindeki gerçekleşmelerini gösterir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir şeyin üstünü başka bir şeyle kapatıp görünmesini engelleyen genel çekirdek için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Örtme işlemini ve görünürlüğün engellenmesi sonucunu birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Zırhın giysiyle veya külün toprakla kaplanması gibi somut bağlamlarda doğal bir karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Somut bir nesnenin üstünün kapatılması işlemini eksiksiz korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Güneş ışığının yıldızları görünmez kıldığı göksel bağlamda sonuç odaklı doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Görsel örtmenin görünürlüğü ortadan kaldıran sonucunu korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal zırh, silah, kül ve güneş ışığı gibi belirli gerçekleşmeleri de taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal haber veya tanıklığı gizleme ve örtü adı gibi daha geniş kullanımlara da uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalın çekirdeğinde bir şeyi örterek görünmesini engelleme vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Çekirdek büyük ölçüde örtüşür; ancak komşu dal soyut gizlemeyi ve örtü nesnelerini de kapsarken bu dalın kanıtı belirli somut ve görsel gerçekleşmelere dayanır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; genel örtme dalı en yakın karışma olasılığını taşıdığı için yayımlandı, öteki adaylar yalnızca örnek veya ortak senaryo düzeyinde kaldı.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه ستر الشيء وتغطيته وكفر الدرع بثوب وتغطية السلاح والرماد المكفور وستر الشمس النجوم والسحاب الشمس

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi karanlık geceyi, denizi, büyük ırmağı, gün batımını ve bulutu aynı adlandırma çevresinde toplar; bunların tümünü tek bir gerçek 'kuşatan örtü' türü saymak yerine, karanlık, genişlik veya kapatma etkisiyle örten farklı varlıklar olarak anlamak gerekir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal genel karanlık ya da genel su kütlesi değildir; kaynakta örtücü etkisiyle adlandırılan belirli varlıklarla sınırlıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın dal, kaynakta doğrudan adlandırılan gece, deniz, büyük ırmak, gün batımı ve bulut kapsamıyla tanımlanır; yapıya özgü başka anlam eklenmez.

concept_map.definition: Karanlığı, genişliği veya kapatma etkisi nedeniyle kişileri ya da görünümü örten karanlık gece, deniz, büyük ırmak, gün batımı veya bulut için kullanılan bir nitelemedir.

facets.statement: Karanlık, genişlik ya da kapatma etkisiyle başka şeylerin görünmesini veya seçilmesini engelleyen varlık.
